title: Distance across time is native: the cut length is the ring graph's distance, the time length the contact graph's directed distance
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: In networks of rule-60 rings, a route isolated by freezing makes its far contact first need the near ring at lag g L + 1, additively, so counted length is native (A40); the earliest need any freeze allows is g delta + 1, delta the directed contact-graph distance, and the most disjoint cuts separating two rings is their ring-graph distance. Without freezing, the first need is that light cone filtered by the parity of shortest routes, not a metric.
